papers.title: Gamma-ray burst minimum variability timescales with Fermi/GBM
papers.classification: sample-member row (MVT population study) - THE MOST RECENT ANALYSIS, hence the Phase-3b default comparison frame
papers.definition_to_carry_T3: Their headline MVT = FWHM_min, 'the full width at half maximum (FWHM) of the narrowest pulse in the light curve', narrowest pulse identified by MEPSA. Their Sect. 2 lists THREE distinct estimators - (i) FWHM_min, (ii) Golkhou+2015/Veres+2023 wavelet dt_min, (iii) MEPSA detection timescale dt_det. Table 1's FWHM column is (i). Never diff across estimators. Npeaks = number of MEPSA-identified peaks. Class per VizieR Note (1): I / II / SEE.
papers.chained_value_flag_T6: their t90 = 22.784 is IDENTICAL to the GBM catalog - chained, not independent. FWHM, Npeaks and Class ARE their own.
papers.why_it_matters_here: Npeaks = 1.0 is an INDEPENDENT, PUBLISHED, AUTOMATED confirmation that this is a single-pulse burst - external validation of its membership in our sample, from a method (MEPSA) unrelated to ours. And MVT = 8.4 s against T90 = 22.8 s says the narrowest structure is >1/3 of the burst: a smooth, unstructured event.

finding: NO DEDICATED-ANALYSIS PAPER EXISTS for GRB 150630223, and ZERO GCN CIRCULARS were ever issued for it - a verified null on both counts, with a same-session control proving the circular archive was alive. The four-form ADS query returned ZERO on all four forms; the entire refereed footprint (3 papers) was recovered by VizieR row lookups and by construction, never by ADS full-text, and a token scan of all 178 corpus PDFs found the burst printed in NONE of them. The footprint is: von Kienlin+2020 (4th GBM catalog, 4 machine-readable rows - durations, fluences, identity, and the K/IA/Mo multi-instrument detection), Poolakkil+2021 (GBM spectral catalog - the ONLY published spectral fits, distributed via HEASARC), and Maccary+2025 (MVT, the Phase-3b latest frame). THREE facts dominate what we inherit. (1) The published spectral picture is a near-featureless SOFT POWER LAW: the catalog's declared best model is PL in BOTH the time-integrated (index -1.876 +/- 0.013) and peak-flux (index -1.913 +/- 0.028) fits, with Ep unconstrained in every curved model (CPL 814 +/- 365, Band 757 +/- 710, SBPL break 2239 +/- 20084 keV) - and the catalog menu contains no additive component at all, so it is silent about, not evidence against, a blackbody. (2) Maccary+2025's MEPSA peak-finder returns Npeaks = 1 with MVT = 8.4 s against T90 = 22.8 s - independent published confirmation of a smooth single pulse, exactly our sample definition. (3) THE DOMINANT HAZARD IS NOT LITERATURE BUT GEOMETRY: at the GBM catalog position the source crossed the Earth's geometric limb at T0-5.2 s and sits only 0.16-1.72 deg above it across the whole stamped window (line-of-sight tangent height climbing 7 -> 78 km), while the ENTIRE pre-burst background window is taken with the source occulted. A systematic whose strength falls monotonically across exactly our source window can mimic both a FRED rise and a hard-to-soft evolution. The GBM team did NOT flag this burst for partial Earth occultation, and GBM plainly saw a bright 24 ph/cm2/s pulse that a 13 km tangent height could not transmit - most likely meaning the true position is several degrees further from the limb than the catalog position (systematic ~3-4 deg vs the quoted 1.46 deg statistical). Recorded as a named alternative hypothesis with falsification tests in P0, not resolved. No redshift, no afterglow, no host, no model advocacy of any kind: a clean null-streak baseline burst whose time-resolved spectroscopy has no published counterpart.
